arxiv-2107-00011.title: Complexity of Supersymmetric Systems and the (co)Homology Problem
arxiv-2107-00011.creator: Chris Cade, P. Marcos Crichigno
arxiv-2107-00011.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chris Cade, P. Marcos Crichigno. We consider the complexity of the local Hamiltonian problem in the context of fermionic Hamiltonians with 𝒩 = 2 \mathcal{N}=2 supersymmetry and show that the problem remains 𝖰𝖬𝖠 {\mathsf{QMA}} -complete. Our main motivation for studying this is the well-known fact that the ground state energy of a supersymmetric system is exactly zero if and only if a certain cohomology group is nontrivial.

arxiv-2206-14917.title: Towards out of distribution generalization for problems in mechanics
arxiv-2206-14917.creator: Lingxiao Yuan, Harold S. Park, Emma Lejeune
arxiv-2206-14917.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Lingxiao Yuan, Harold S. Park, Emma Lejeune. There has been a massive increase in research interest towards applying data driven methods to problems in mechanics, with a particular emphasis on using data driven methods for predictive modeling and design of materials with novel functionality. While traditional machine learning (ML) methods have enabled many breakthroughs, they rely on the assumption that the training (observed) data and testing (unseen) data are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d).

arxiv-2309-11800.title: AT2022cmc: a Tidal Disruption Event with Two-component Jet in a Bondi-profile Circumnuclear Medium
arxiv-2309-11800.creator: Chang Zhou, Zi-Pei Zhu, Wei-Hua Lei, Shao-Yu Fu, Wei Xie, Dong Xu
arxiv-2309-11800.description: Abstract A supermassive black hole can launch a relativistic jet when it violently disrupts a star that passes too close. Such jetted tidal disruption events (TDEs) are rare and unique tools to investigate quiescent supermassive black holes, jet physics, and circumnuclear environment at high redshift. arxiv-2410-08014.title: Privacy-preserved LLM Cascade via CoT-enhanced Policy Learning
arxiv-2410-08014.creator: Kai Zhang, Congchao Wang, Liqian Peng, Alec Go, Xiaozhong Liu
arxiv-2410-08014.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have gained significant attention in on-device applications due to their remarkable performance across real-world tasks. However, on-device LLMs often suffer from suboptimal performance due to hardware limitations. A promising solution to this challenge is cascading a weaker local (on-device) LLM with a more powerful server LLM.

arxiv-2410-09682.title: General Constrained Matrix Optimization
arxiv-2410-09682.creator: Casey Garner, Gilad Lerman, Shuzhong Zhang
arxiv-2410-09682.description: Abstract This paper presents and analyzes the first matrix optimization model which allows general coordinate and spectral constraints. The breadth of problems our model covers is exemplified by a lengthy list of examples from the literature, including semidefinite programming, matrix completion, and quadratically constrained quadratic programs (QCQPs), and we demonstrate our model enables completely novel formulations of numerous problems.

arxiv-2503-23144.title: A low-cost four-component relativistic coupled cluster linear response theory based on perturbation sensitive natural spinors
arxiv-2503-23144.creator: Sudipta Chakraborty, Amrita Manna, T. Daniel Crawford, Achintya Kumar Dutta
arxiv-2503-23144.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sudipta Chakraborty, Amrita Manna, T. Daniel Crawford, Achintya Kumar Dutta. We present an efficient implementation of four-component linear response coupled cluster singles and doubles (4c-LRCCSD) theory that enables accurate and computationally efficient calculation of polarizabilities for systems containing heavy elements. We have observed that the frozen natural spinor (FNS)-based truncation scheme is not suitable for linear response properties, as it leads to larger errors in static and dynamic polarizability values.

arxiv-2511-15742.title: Sequential testing problem: A follow-up review Journal: Discrete Applied Mathematics
arxiv-2511-15742.creator: Tonguç Ünlüyurt
arxiv-2511-15742.description: Abstract This review aims to provide a comprehensive update on the progress made on the Sequential Testing problem (STP) in the last 20 years after the review, [ 78 ] was published. Many studies have provided new theoretical results, extensions of the problem, and new applications.

arxiv-2602-09649.description: Abstract Ancestral recombination graphs (ARGs) capture the full genetic history of samples from a recombining species. Although ARGs have been a central theoretical object in population genetics for decades, their practical use was constrained by the lack of scalable inference methods, standard interchange formats, and software infrastructure.

pmc-11460054.creator: M. C. de Ruiter, L.-M. van Klaveren, V. G. M. Geukers
pmc-11460054.description: The Lancet Global Independent Commission has called for a systems-based approach to health professions education. pmc-11653362.description: BackgroundPsychiatric disorders is a major public health problem and epilepsy contributes significantly to depression. We aimed to explore the relationship between dietary patterns and mental illness in patients with epilepsy.MethodsThe data presented here are based on the 2013–2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES).

pmc-12542072.title: MiR-877, an exosomal miRNA from mechanical stretch induced adipose derived stromal cells, enhances fracture healing in nonunion rats with type 2 diabetes mellitus
pmc-12542072.creator: Liang Tian, Dong Zhang, Zheng Wang, Junwei Su, Changjiang Liu, Chao Jian, Aixi Yu
pmc-12542072.description: BackgroundBone nonunion or delayed union is a serious complication in diabetic patients with fractures, urgently requiring novel therapeutic strategies. Exosomes derived from stromal cells are naturally occurring nanoparticles carrying bioactive molecules that mediate intercellular communication and play crucial roles in diabetic fracture repair. Importantly, mechanical stimuli can modulate the cargo composition of exosomes, influencing bone healing outcomes.

pmc-13085079.title: The response of broilers to xylanase and β-glucanase combination in maize-based diets containing wheat distillers’ dried grain with solubles
pmc-13085079.creator: Eunjoo Kim, Mingan Choct, Anna Fickler, Leon Hall, Tamsyn M. Crowley, Nishchal K. Sharma
pmc-13085079.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Broiler diets containing wheat distillers’ dried grain with solubles (wDDGS) have higher levels of non-starch polysaccharides (NSP) compared to conventional maize-soybean meal-based diets, which can increase intestinal viscosity and impair nutrient utilisation. This study investigated the effects of supplemental xylanase and β-glucanase (XG) preparation on growth performance, ileal flow of soluble NSP constituent sugars, and the gastrointestinal environment in broilers fed maize-based diets with varying wDDGS levels.

pmc-13214141.title: Clinical management of Xpert® MTB/RIF ultra trace results among presumptive tuberculosis patients in Lebanon: a retrospective observational study
pmc-13214141.creator: Marianne Antar Soutou, Sirine Abou Ismail, Anne-Marie Farhat, Soukaina Basma, Laurent Raskine, François-Xavier Babin, Farah Jradi, Hiam Yaacoub, Marianne Abifadel, Josette Najjar-Pellet
pmc-13214141.description: BackgroundInterpreting trace results from the Xpert® MTB/RIF Ultra assay, a frontline diagnostic tool for tuberculosis, remains challenging, particularly in low-tuberculosis burden settings. This study aimed to provide practical recommendations for managing trace-positive patients in Lebanon based on clinical, radiological, and bacteriological data.

pmc-13393060.title: Promoting breastfeeding through digital communication: a longitudinal randomized controlled trial
pmc-13393060.creator: Margherita Guidetti, Giulia Scaglioni, Nicoletta Cavazza, Rossana Reggiani, Ramona Infante, Maria Teresa Molinazzi, Isabella Neri
pmc-13393060.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionBreastfeeding is a key early-life primary prevention behavior; yet, despite consistent recommendations and recent improvements, exclusive breastfeeding rates remain well below target levels. This preregistered longitudinal randomized controlled trial (RCT) tested the effectiveness of two resource-efficient digital communication interventions.MethodsWomen in the 36th week of pregnancy (N = 467) were randomly assigned to one of six conditions in a 2 × 3 between-participants design. The first intervention consisted of informational messages targeting components of the extended Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB).

pmc-13444102.description: The functional impact of a large portion of the human genome known as “dark matter DNA”, which is composed mainly of repeat sequences, remains unknown. The genome also encodes many putative and poorly characterized transcription factors. Here, we determine genomic binding locations of 166 poorly characterized human transcription factors in living cells.

pmc-13586648.title: Consistent root microbiomes across contrasting habitats in a wild perennial vine
pmc-13586648.creator: K. Aleklett, K. Karlsson Green, C. B. Andersen, N. Ramirez, D. Kadish, L. Grenville‐Briggs, Å. Lankinen
pmc-13586648.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026).
